A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STAD research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original adaptation experiments on temporal shifts, reproduction datasets, and synthetic corruptions, together with ablations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds PACS, ImageNet-C, supervised-oracle comparisons, and further sensitivity and runtime results.

M1.justification: The Gaussian/vMF prototype-tracking architecture and sliding-window EM design remain. The written vMF updates change: v3 fixes the normalization of the update vector and includes t=1 in the emission-concentration sum (v2 Eqs. 25–26 and 30; v3 Eqs. 36–37 and 41). These are limited procedural corrections; expanded Gaussian documentation does not establish a new method.

E1.justification: v3 adds PACS, covering photo, art-painting, cartoon, and sketch domains under held-out-domain and sequential abrupt-shift scenarios. It also adds ImageNet-C corruption evaluation. The six datasets evaluated in v2 remain.

E2.justification: RoTTA is newly evaluated in Tables 2–4 and the temporal and batch-size plots; CMF is added to Table 2. Appendix D.5 adds a supervised fine-tuning reference. These substantially broaden comparisons beyond v2's baseline set.

E3.justification: New PACS protocols use either three training domains with a rotating held-out domain or photo-only training followed by sequential adaptation. ImageNet-C introduces ViT-Base evaluation. The supervised reference uses a separate labeled split sized at 10% of the adaptation stream and one fine-tuning epoch per timestep. Existing benchmark settings largely remain.

E4.justification: v3 tests robustness to non-gradual PACS shifts, adds supervised-oracle headroom analysis, extends hyperparameter sensitivity from Yearbook to CIFAR-10-C, and expands runtime analysis to ImageNetV2. The original dynamics ablation, cluster-fidelity analysis, and BN-combination experiment are retained.

E5.justification: Error bars in v2 Figures 4–5 are removed from corresponding v3 Figures 3–4, substantially reducing uncertainty information for temporal trajectories and batch-size sensitivity. Table 3 also loses its explicit three-random-data-seed statement. Aggregate uncertainty entries and cluster-fidelity error bars remain; changed run counts are not established.

E6.justification: New results include STAD-vMF's 60.80% sequential PACS mean, 51.50% ImageNet-C mean, and the supervised oracle's 90.67% Yearbook accuracy. Comparator and sensitivity results also expand. Original STAD accuracy entries remain, but its relative FMoW-Time runtime changes from 30.8 to 8.8 (v2 Table 9; v3 Table 13), without an explanation establishing the cause.

T1.justification: v3 adds extensive Gaussian filtering, smoothing, and EM derivations in Appendix B.1, revises the vMF normalization and emission-sum equations, and explicitly handles temporal boundaries. Section 2 drops the formal bounded-discrepancy condition between consecutive distributions, although qualitative gradual-shift assumptions remain.

C1.justification: The central claims about unsupervised dynamic prototypes, difficult temporal shifts, and robustness to label shift and small batches remain. The introduction's empirical contribution now explicitly emphasizes applicability beyond temporal shifts, including domain-adaptation benchmarks, while the conclusion qualifies where STAD is most effective.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses dependence on persistent prototype correlation and possible silent degradation from unsupervised prototype drift. It interprets the new PACS and oracle experiments in terms of applicability beyond gradual shifts and remaining supervised headroom. Existing explanations of label-shift benefits and feature-extractor limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: The Gaussian inference equations and algorithm substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v2's brief specification. v3 also documents RoTTA search ranges and defaults, the ViT-Base source and representation dimension, DomainBed-based PACS training, and the supervised-reference procedure. The expanded SAR discussion clarifies an already reported BN setting.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning through a taxonomy of realistic TTA settings and discussions of temporal domain generalization and gradual domain adaptation. Section 4 adds distinctions from Lee and Chang's SSM-based update filtering and Dai and Yang's static EM prototype adaptation. These are substantive additions beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Dataset descriptions move from Section 5 to Appendix C.1, the method appendices are consolidated under Appendix B, and expanded related work becomes Appendix A. Problem-setting and inference explanations are reworked, the conclusion becomes a discussion, and a broader-impact statement and journal front matter are added.

P2.justification: v3 substantially revises the document layout, expands comparison tables, adds benchmark tables and an oracle figure, and reorganizes sensitivity tables. The graphical model moves from v2 Figure 2 to v3 Figure 6. Existing plots are redrawn with revised colors, legends, comparator curves, and uncertainty displays; the cluster plot and ablation table receive more space.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessment of STAD's applicability through abrupt-shift tests, additional comparators, and a supervised reference, while expanded inference documentation addresses gaps in v2. These gains are tempered by removed error bars and unreconciled prose: Section 5.2 still says no method improves on ImageNetV2's source model, although Table 3 adds RoTTA's higher mean, 63.39 versus 63.18. The net quality gain is positive but limited.
